subject: RRO or R: which one I am using?

messages.author: cce19e1de16efdda
messages.subject: RRO or R: which one I am using?
parts:
Hi there, I know the question seems silly, but after some emails exchange with the guys at support they advised me to write the question here so everyone could see it. Here is the situation:

I Installed RRO on my mac (Mavericks 10.9.5). Now in my Application folder I have two icons, the typical R console icon and the funny monkey for RRO. When I open one or the other I get exactly the same starting message, which is the Console screen capture I attached in this email. Note that I get this when I click the monkey symbol even though what I understand from the RR website is that RRO 3.1.2 is on its way, but still not available. 

Overall, I am not entirely sure that I am using RRO. Should I remove the "old" R Console icon? How do I know which R I am using (R or RRO)?

If is of any help, if the order of events is: install RRO then install R3.1.2 the starting message when clicking any of the two icons starts with "R version 3.1.2"
                          if the order of events is: install R3.1.2 and then RRO the starting message when clicking any of the two icons starts with "R version 3.1.1"

So it seems that the last installation overwrites the former one. However, independently of what is the order of the events described before, the starting message includes:
"Revolution R Open 8.0 beta
The enhanced R distribution from Revolution Analytics
Visit mran.revolutionanalytics.com/open for information
about additional features and technical support options."

So well, how do I know whether I am using "normal R" or i am into the Revolution!

messages.author: 0eb5a09fd4de9e5e
messages.subject: Re: RRO or R: which one I am using?
parts:
Hi, Javier

Thank you for posting more information about your problem here.  You have now provided additional information in your very clear report.

I suspect that your issue is similar to https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO/issues/45 and I have updated the existing issue with your new information.

I will ask the team to attempt to replicate this behaviour on a Mac.

I apologise for the confusion this has created.  I suspect the following:

- You are running CRAN R-3.1.2
- Because RRO and R install in the same framework on a Mac, you still have some artefacts of RRO in the R folder, in particular the Rprofile.site file, where this message originates

Hopefully we can post additional advice soon.  Meanwhile, if you want a completely clean installation, you may have to uninstall both R and RRO, then re-install only the version you actually want to use.

Regards

Andrie

messages.author: 88275a537c4bd7d2
messages.subject: Re: RRO or R: which one I am using?
parts:
Hi Javier,

Yes, if you run

rm -rf /Library/Frameworks/R.framework

it will delete any packages you installed with CRAN R and you'll need to reinstall them. Note that if you use "checkpoint" packages are installed locally to the project folder, so it won't affect any of those as you upgrade to new versions of RRO.

Making the version-to-version transition is something we aim to make easier with RRO, especially with regard to packages, so please keep the feedback and suggestions coming!

Hope this helps,
# David Smith
